differences_from_lex: KV_TOKENS/KV_PORT/KV_DB/KV_HOST environment variables -> --tokens flag and the skeleton's --port; no KV_DB and no KV_HOST
no SQLite: state is in memory for the life of the process, nothing persists across restarts (brief says so)
'listens on loopback by default' dropped: a cancho listener binds all interfaces and has no --host; the attack's loopback check is removed
'every query is parameterized' replaced by its behavioural half: SQL-looking prefixes/keys and % _ are never wildcards (400 / literal)
no lex-web/lex-schema/lex-orm: std.http, std.json, skeleton are the toolbox

added to the brief (the Lex one left them open): 405 for a known path with another method, 404 for unknown paths, order of checks (401, 405, 413, key, body), prefix is percent-decoded before validation, key in the path is not percent-decoded, duplicate JSON fields are 400, ttl_seconds null/float/string/out of range is 400, value length counts code points, tenant names are prefixes of each other share nothing, fixed-capacity store with 507 and a no-leak requirement (10000 replacements of one key)
dropped from the Lex attack: 'listens on loopback only', the 'trailing space' check is kept but accepts 401 or 404 because an HTTP parser may trim header whitespace
pitfalls: a borrowed App (&!a App) cannot give up a std.map/std.vec/std.buffer field and take a grown one back (app.m = map.put(heap, app.m, ..) is 'expected Map, found &!a Map'), and `borrow mut app.f as ...` is not syntax; so a growable collection cannot live in App. The reference allocates fixed Boxes once (hash table of row numbers, row table, byte arena) and mutates them through contents(app.f); growth is replaced by a documented capacity and compaction
every helper that takes `app: &!a App` needs `[&a]` in its generics, and a function that declares [heap] must really use the heap (app_new must allocate)
a region arena is 64 KiB: json tapes (3 ints per node, tape_len of a 4 KiB body is ~100 KiB) must be box_slice on the heap, not alloc_slice
JSON string length must be counted in code points (json.string_into then utf8.count), not bytes; a 1000-character value can be 4000 bytes, and the body limit is 4096 bytes
python http.client json.dumps escapes non-ASCII to \uXXXX (6 bytes each): the attack sends raw UTF-8 for the 2-byte and 4-byte character checks
an early-exit token compare is not observable; the attack checks the neighbours instead (prefix of a token, token with a suffix, two spaces)
std.map.hash is public and usable for an own table; tombstones in an open-addressed table need a rebuild or the probe loop never ends
no `break`/`continue`; negative literals are written 0 - 1 in existing code but -1 also parses
